one_liner: C++20 driver for the Tegra X1 NVJPG hardware JPEG decoder; README shows 3-4x lower latency than libjpeg-turbo on the A57 cores.
what_it_does: Decodes baseline JPEGs on the Tegra X1's fixed-function NVJPG block by talking to it directly through Host1x channel ioctls: NVIDIA's downstream nvhost/nvmap device nodes on L4T Linux, or libnx nvdrv on Nintendo Switch homebrew. The API is its own, not libjpeg's: build an nj::Image from a path, fd, FILE* or byte vector and call parse() (header-only parse of SOF/DQT/DHT/DRI/SOS), allocate an nj::Surface (RGB, BGR, RGBA, BGRA, ABGR, ARGB, pitch-linear) or nj::VideoSurface (planar YUV 4:2:0/4:2:2/4:4:4), then Decoder::render(image, surface, alpha, downscale) and Decoder::wait(surface). Decode only; no encoder.
how_it_is_fast: The CPU only parses the JPEG headers, copies the entropy-coded scan data into a DMA buffer and fills a 0xb2c-byte picture-info block (Huffman and quantization tables, sampling, pitches); Huffman decoding, IDCT, chroma upsampling, YUV-to-RGB conversion (fixed-point BT.601, BT.709 or full-range JFIF kernels) and power-of-two downscaling (1/2, 1/4, 1/8) all run in the NVJPG hardware. Work is submitted as a Host1x command buffer and completion is signalled by a syncpoint fence, and Decoder::initialize(num_ring_entries) keeps a ring of submission slots so the CPU can parse and queue the next image while the hardware decodes. The speedup comes from dedicated silicon, not from a better software algorithm.
when_to_use: Nintendo Switch homebrew (devkitA64, libnx) that loads many baseline JPEG icons, thumbnails or screenshots and wants the Cortex-A57 cores free; the Switch menu sphaira uses it (issue #1).

Tegra X1 boards running NVIDIA's L4T kernel, where /dev/nvhost-nvjpg, /dev/nvhost-ctrl and /dev/nvmap exist and you need lower per-image decode latency than libjpeg-turbo on the A57 (README: about 3x on a 720x1080 file, about 4x on 3200x1800).
Pipelines that hand the decoded image straight to the GPU: Surface::to_deko3d wraps the output buffer as a deko3d texture without a copy.
Thumbnail generation where hardware downscale by 2, 4 or 8 and hardware YUV-to-RGB conversion replace CPU passes.
when_not_to_use: Any hardware other than the Tegra X1: it programs the NVJPG engine directly, and on Linux it needs NVIDIA's downstream nvhost/nvmap UAPI, not mainline host1x.
Progressive, arithmetic-coded or lossless JPEGs, CMYK or other 4-component files, and files whose component ids are 4 or higher (Adobe-style 'R','G','B' ids) all return an error.
Untrusted input: the header parser does not bound DHT symbol counts or table ids (see gotchas), so a malformed file can write past fixed-size arrays.
Workloads that read decoded pixels back on the CPU: surfaces are allocated non-CPU-cacheable, which suits GPU consumers but makes CPU reads slow.
Projects that cannot take GPL-3.0 code, or that need active maintenance: the only changes since 2022 are two 2025 fixes prompted by one downstream user.

integration.form: static lib (meson default_library=static, or libnvjpg.a from the devkitA64 Makefile)
integration.dependencies: Linux: NVIDIA L4T kernel device nodes /dev/nvmap, /dev/nvhost-ctrl, /dev/nvhost-nvjpg (SDL2 only for the examples). Switch: libnx (nvdrv and mmu services), deko3d optional for the texture-export path and examples.
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 (gnu++20; uses concepts, requires-clauses and the GNU case-range extension), so GCC with GNU extensions; devkitA64 for Switch, meson for Linux
integration.platforms: aarch64 Tegra X1 only (Nintendo Switch under Horizon with libnx, or Tegra X1 under NVIDIA L4T Linux)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; nvmap and nvhost-ctrl file descriptors are process-wide statics and a Decoder's ring iterator is unsynchronized, so use one Decoder per thread

gotchas: Parser memory safety (lib/image.cpp): parse_dht reads sum(codes) symbols, up to 4080, into a 162-byte array and indexes 4-entry table arrays with a 4-bit id (up to 15); parse_dqt does the same for quantization ids; table ids from SOF and SOS are never range-checked. parse_dqt also computes precision as `info >> 8` on a uint8_t, which is always 0, so 16-bit quantization tables are misread. Image(path) opens a file descriptor that is never closed, and a short read() is not detected.

History: component ids were assumed 1-based until commit 16c10a3 (2025-06-09, issue #1: a 4:4:4 Switch icon decoded to garbage), and parse() could loop forever on non-JPEG input until PR #2 (2025-06-18). In that PR the author says his FFmpeg 'envideo' hwaccel (averne/FFmpeg, envideo_mjpeg.c) 'handles surface formats correctly, aborts on some hardware issues', which this library does not.

The scan-data buffer defaults to 5 MiB per ring entry (Decoder::initialize capacity 0x500000); larger scans fail with ENOMEM until Decoder::resize is called. Output pitch is aligned to 256 bytes, so rows are not tightly packed.

On Switch, nj::initialize() temporarily sets __nx_applet_type to LibraryApplet to obtain nvdrv:a/s/t, and on Linux NJ_TRY_ERRNO tests errno without clearing it first, so a stale errno from an earlier unrelated call makes initialize fail.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over libjpeg-turbo, jpeg-nitro or zenjpeg only when you are on Tegra X1 (Switch or L4T) with trusted baseline JPEGs and want the decode off the CPU; those siblings are portable CPU decoders, and GPUJPEG targets CUDA GPUs, not the X1's NVJPG block.
verified_claims_summary: First-party README table: one image decoded to an RGB surface, averaged over 1000 iterations, on a Tegra X1 with its Cortex-A57 at max 2.091 GHz; NVJPG 2.036 ms vs libjpeg-turbo 6.127 ms for a 70 KiB 720x1080 file and 15.997 vs 66.341 ms for a 1.6 MiB 3200x1800 file (about 3.0x and 4.1x, derived from page data). The table was already in the README by 2021-02-08, before the Horizon port (2021-03-08), the hardware-definition corrections and both 2025 fixes, so it was measured on the early Linux build and never re-run; the timing harness, libjpeg-turbo version and build, NVJPG clock rate and timed region are not published (the shipped examples time one render plus wait, i.e. scan copy plus hardware decode, after header parsing).
status_note: Stale since 2025-06-18 (23 commits, 19 stars, no open issues or PRs); about 1.5k lines of GPL-3.0 C++20 that can be vendored, but it only runs on Tegra X1 with libnx or NVIDIA's downstream L4T kernel, and its parser should not see untrusted files.
